record._scope: A reusable treatment for marking anything in a composition that does not match what ships. Defined once here so the remaining fourteen compositions follow it.
record.problem: Compositions render known defects accurately and distinguish them only in prose. A reader scanning a frame cannot tell a defect from an intentional pattern.
record.colourConstraint: The marker may not use red, yellow, orange or green. Marked content is frequently red/yellow/green alerts, chips and status indicators, so a semantic colour would collide. The marker must read as chrome, clearly outside the thing it marks.

treatment.container: Auto-layout VERTICAL, itemSpacing 12, padding 16, cornerRadius 4, strokeWeight 1, dashPattern [6,4]

record.structure: Example FIRST, then a header row (chip label + one-line "Fix lives in ..."), then a one-line statement of the difference. The example leads so that a marked example and an unmarked one in the same row share a baseline — with the chip above, a marked cell pushed its example 80-190px below its unmarked siblings.

labels.GAP: the component cannot express it at all — not a rendering difference

record.rule: Any example rendering something that does not match what ships sits inside a marker. Correct examples sit outside it. The distinction must be legible without reading a word.
record.legend: Every composition using markers carries one line in its header block explaining the dashed panel, so the frame is self-describing.

marked: standard/success cell — no standardSuccess rule in AlertOverrides, renders as a tinted card unlike its three siblings
outlined row (all four severities) — no outlined rules in AlertOverrides, low contrast; only one outlined Alert exists in the entire codebase, which bears on whether it is worth fixing
AlertTitle — renders Akkurat LL Bold 700 because typography.ts registers only 400 and 700 where MUI styles AlertTitle at 500
two close-icon-button examples — Icon button Small is 34px where code ships a 28px box
two-action fragment (GAP) — the action slot is a single INSTANCE_SWAP where code takes a fragment; 9 production slots hold two interactive elements
appliedFirstIn.unmarkedBecauseResolved: The teal Button on filled alerts was a defect in the prior pass. It is resolved by buttonInheritColour2026_08_28, rebuilt with color=inherit, and now sits outside any marker.
appliedFirstIn.residual: In the severity grid, standard and filled rows render examples at 334px while the outlined row renders at 358px, because the outlined row is wrapped as ONE row-level marker rather than four per-cell markers. Per-cell insets there would nest a marker inside a marker. Left as-is.

alertMessageDefault.change: Alert's Message default changed from "This is an info message." to "This is an alert message."
alertMessageDefault.why: The old default handed a designer text saying 'info' on warning, error and success alerts.
alertMessageDefault.constraint: Per-severity copy is NOT expressible. Figma variant sets share one default per TEXT property, so all 12 variants show the same placeholder unless Message is unbound from the variants. A severity-neutral default was used instead.
alertMessageDefault.geometry: 0 of 12 variants changed size or position; set remains 1800x224.

record.rowAlignment: In any row mixing marked and unmarked examples, the unmarked ones sit in a transparent "Inset — unmarked" frame with padding identical to the marker (16), and each column groups its caption+note into a "Text block" set to the row max height. Both are required: the inset equalises the example inset, the text block equalises what sits above it. Verified by measuring absolute Y of every example in the row, not by structural assertion.
record.widthBehaviour: A marker fills its column; the column is sized to the content. A single-example panel must not inherit a full section width - the Title panel spanned 1536 only because its sibling column had been deleted, leaving one column at full width.
